name: Learn simple calligraphy
blurb: One hand — italic or foundational — learned properly. Calligraphy is about consistent angle, consistent spacing and slow deliberate strokes.
gear: A broad-edge pen: a dip nib or a calligraphy fountain pen
steps: Choose one hand and stick to it. Italic is the most useful for everyday writing.
Set the pen angle — usually 45 degrees for italic — and hold it constant. This single variable creates the thick and thin strokes.
Learn the basic strokes before any letters: the stem, the arch, the branch, the o-shape.
Learn letters in family groups that share a construction, not in alphabetical order.
Learn the x-height and stick to the guidelines. Consistency of height and slant is what makes it look professional.
Practise spacing with whole words, then write a full quotation as a finished piece.
tips: Draw the letters slowly. Calligraphy is drawing, not handwriting, and speed comes only after the shapes are automatic.
A wandering pen angle is the fault behind nearly every wobbly beginner alphabet.
proof: A finished piece with even spacing, consistent angle and a straight baseline, that you would frame.
